Reading chosen: dynamic error when blocked (clause 20.1). Tests the blocked case: only non-matching message queued, no timers running; the new-snapshot case is covered by 20.05.01_test_010/011.
No syntax exists to activate a default in another component, so a behavioural test is used: a default activated by a PTC has no effect in the MTC.
Reading 1 (implicit deactivation at MTC/test case termination). Observed indirectly: a default activated in one test case is not active in the next test case.

Whether a default is suspended is in general only known at runtime, so the violation (re-activating an active default) is expected to cause a runtime error rather than a compile-time rejection.
No syntax exists to deactivate a default of another component; behavioural test: MTC 'deactivate' does not affect a default activated in the PTC.
Default false (removal) is observed by re-activating the reference afterwards, which must be a runtime error (restriction e of 20.5.2) because the default was removed rather than suspended.
Use of an uninitialized variable is treated as a runtime error (ttcn3verdict:error) since initialization is not decidable statically in general.
